_readme: Engine part of the analysis spec: the claims table every kind embeds (marker CLAIMS in a method's kinds.json), the critic and gate kinds. Method kinds live in methods/<m>/kinds.json.

Field types: s=string, i=integer, b=boolean, l=list (';'-separated in Markdown), n=nullable string. Long form: {"t": "s", "enum": [...], "req": true}. `$scoring.critics` etc. resolve against the merged run configuration.
conventions:
no '|' inside cells (use '/'), no line breaks inside cells (use
), lists separated by ';', enum tokens English exactly as given, free text in the deliverable language

assumptions._readme: opt-in section (marker ASSUMPTIONS in a method's kinds.json; key assumptions_taken, so it never collides with a method's own `assumptions` table): the readings an autonomous run takes instead of leaving a question open; `dbcx questions import <scope>` registers each row as a client-directed assumption (A-nn on the Annahmen sheet with the confirm/deny dropdown)
assumptions.heading: Assumptions taken
assumptions.help: Never leave a question open: take the most probable reading (a tie -> the lowest effort, closest to the standard) and record it here. id = a short local id (AS-01); affects = the row keys the reading moves (FR-041 or FR-041@<option>); question = the open point as the client would be asked it; reading_taken = the reading you proceed under (short); assumption = the sentence the client confirms or denies, in the deliverable language ('Die Schätzung geht davon aus, dass ...'); why = why this reading is the most probable; if_not = what changes when the client denies it; alternatives = the other readings (';'-separated). Also write the short reading into the affected row's own assumption text.

claims.heading: Claims
claims.help: Every statement that ends up in a deliverable. ONE PROPOSITION PER CLAIM: one fact or one judgement, at most two figures (a count and its denominator or basis), one `target` sheet - a paragraph carrying several figures is split into several claims (a wrong figure then costs one atom, not the paragraph). type = fact | assessment. evidence = evidence locators (repository path[:line-range], corpus locator SRC-nnn#p12, workbook Sheet!A12, URL, or PS-7-NNN reference id) separated by ';'. A locator is an ADDRESS A TOOL RESOLVES, not prose: no ellipsis ('.../file.xml'), no scheme prefix ('vendor:...'), no parenthetical or comment inside the cell ('file.xml (fully read)', 'PS-7-003 (aspects a, b, c)' - a comma inside a cell also splits it into two broken locators), and never a tool invocation ('dbcx count x'). Standard/vendor code is cited by its real path under the checked-out standard code roots. A reference fact is cited by its id alone. Whatever the parenthetical was going to say - that you read the whole file, which directory you searched, the rule behind a count - belongs in the statement or the rationale, where the client reads it. A negative finding still needs a real address: cite the directory you searched, not a path with your conclusion appended. The CHECK warns per cell that does not resolve; a cell a critic cannot open scores 4 at best. An assessment lists the ids of the fact claims it rests on. target = deliverable/sheet plus the row(s) the claim backs, exactly one sheet: `D3/Coverage#FR-012`, `D4/Features#F-001`, `D2/Patched#r1a2b3c4d,r5e6f7a8b` (several rows of ONE sheet separated by ','). The row id is the row's `rid` in the converted .json (the row key itself when it is an id, else a short hash of the key text); the exact key value works too. Coverage is an exact row-id match: a claim backs exactly the rows its target names - never write the row key into the statement to make a row count as covered. A sheet showing one row per scope (e.g. D2/Depth) needs no row id. The statement is written as an absolute, present-tense fact for the client - never 'corrected in round 2', never a date of an edit, never the words round/critic/analyst/orchestrator/session; correction history goes into history (internal, not exported). quote (optional; `claims.quotes` warn | required) = ONE verbatim excerpt of at least 20 characters in the original language, copied from a cited locator, that carries the statement; several fragments of the same locator are joined by ' […] '. Never paraphrase or translate it - `dbcx evidence quotes <scope>` looks it up word for word and the critics see the result. The quote lives in its own column; the evidence cell stays locator-only

critic.title: Gauntlet score: <scope> / <critic> / round <n>
critic.head_help: critic = one of the tokens in run.json scoring.critics (client | standard)

sections.heading: Scores
sections.help: score 0-10 per docs/SCORING.md; ONE row per claim_id; issue and fix_hint mandatory below 8; counter_evidence mandatory for 2 and 4; verdict false = you checked and the statement is contradicted by evidence (blocks the pass regardless of the score); issue on a passing claim = optional wording/precision note (collected, never becomes a rework on its own); a fix_hint that asserts a count names the test that produced it and what the test would miss; accept_if mandatory below the PASS THRESHOLD: the test you will apply next round - what the corrected statement must state or cite to pass (write it before you see the fix; it keeps your judgement independent and tells the analyst what settles the claim); found_via = optional, the tool that found your counter-evidence (grep | search | read | map)

sections.heading: Missing claims
sections.help: one line per missing statement ('- ...'), most important first, at most MISSING CLAIMS CAP; the standard critic prefixes each with [standard-fact] or [inference-requires-client-evidence]

sections.heading: Estate observations
sections.help: one line per fact you established OUTSIDE this scope while scoring (another scope, the whole estate, a standard fact that changes a passed claim elsewhere) - with locator or URL; collected by score_aggregate for the consolidators, the client-attention candidates and the final report. Empty list is fine.

gate.title: Final gate: <persona> / round <n>
gate.head_help: persona = one of the tokens in run.json scoring.gate_personas

sections.heading: Key questions
sections.help: ONE row per KEY QUESTION of your brief, nothing else. score on the anchored scale: 10 = answered on the Management Summary with a figure, its consequence and its basis; 8 = answered in the relevant sheet with at most one filter, the basis visible in each row; 6 = answerable only by combining sheets or reading many rows; 4 = partial or ambiguous; 2 = not answerable; 0 = the deliverable says something wrong or misleading (you name the cell that contradicts another cell or the rendering); odd scores are in-betweens. where = Sheet!Cell where you found the answer (- when none); answer = the answer as you read it, one sentence in the deliverable language; rationale = why this score and not the next anchor up

sections.heading: Board test
sections.help: forward_unchanged = yes | no: would you forward the deliverables to your board exactly as they are; blocking_items = the issue ids (I1; I4) that stop you, empty when yes

sections.heading: What is missing
sections.help: unscored: what you expected to find for your role and did not find, one line each (deliverable language); empty list is fine

sections.heading: Issues
sections.help: no minimum count - only what costs you a point on a key question or blocks the board test; id = I1, I2 ...; deliverable = the workbook file name; location = Sheet!Cell, Sheet!A2:C9 or Sheet/<row id> (one location per issue); kind = content (a statement or figure is missing, wrong or unproven) | presentation (layout, chart, label, order, wording of a cell) | structure (a sheet, column or KPI is missing or in the wrong place) | language (not in the deliverable language, jargon, raw keys) | outside-scope (a wish the study was not commissioned for); severity blocker = you would not forward the deliverable, major = costs a key question at least one anchor, minor = cosmetic; question_id = the key question it hurts; proposed_change = the concrete change, deliverable language

sections.heading: Summary
sections.help: 3-5 sentences, deliverable language: what convinced you, what stops you

sections.heading: Samples
sections.help: one row per sampled row of the SAMPLE file, in its order; location = Sheet!<row> or Sheet/<row id>; statement = the row's claim in one line; locator = what you opened (file:line, [Qn] + URL, A-nn); result: confirmed = the locator shows what the row says; imprecise = right direction, wrong figure/scope/wording; unsupported = the locator does not show it; false = the evidence contradicts it; no-locator = a 'Code' row without a repository locator; assumption-in-code = an 'Annahme' row the code actually settles (name the file:line)

sections.heading: Scores
sections.help: one row per deliverable: 10 = every sampled row confirmed; 8 = at most one imprecise row, nothing false or unsupported; 6 = several imprecise or one unsupported; 4 = more than one unsupported; 2 = a false row on a verdict or figure the client decides on; 0 = several false rows

sections.heading: Defects
sections.help: one row per sample that is not confirmed (id = V1, V2 ...); kind is content for a wrong or unproven statement; evidence = the file:line or URL that shows the truth; severity blocker = false on a verdict or figure, major = unsupported or assumption-in-code, minor = imprecise wording

sections.heading: Summary
sections.help: 3-5 sentences (English, internal): what you checked, what held, what did not

postpass.title: Post-pass justifications: <scope>
postpass.head_help: one file per scope: analysis/gauntlet/<scope>/postpass-justifications.md; rows are kept across post-passes (append, never delete a row)

sections.heading: Justifications
sections.help: ONE row per claim whose statement, evidence or target the post-pass changed: justification = which item required the change and why the scored proposition is unchanged (English, internal); accept_if_kept = how the corrected text still meets the critic's accept_if that `dbcx postpass check` prints for the claim (mandatory when it prints one). A changed scored claim without a row is refused by the check.

claim_rules._readme: Atomic-claim rules checked by md_to_json (WARNING lines, never INVALID): statement length, number of figures (ids, locators, versions and years are not figures), exactly one target of the form D<n>/<Sheet>[:<row id>]; a method may list its allowed target sheets in method.json `claims.targets`. Overridable per run in run.json scoring.claim_max_statement_chars / scoring.claim_max_figures. Evidence: in the first engagement the round-1 failure share rose from 3 % (statements < 300 chars) to 48 % (> 1000 chars) and from 14 % (one figure) to 50 % (seven or more). Row targets (A5): D<n>/<Sheet>#<row id>[,<row id>] or <kind>/<section>#<row id>; the legacy ':' separator is accepted; coverage is an exact row-id match (engine/tools/rows.py).
